tabs.label: Terminal-Bench Science 0.1
captions: Terminal-Bench Science 0.1 tests whether agents can complete scientific research workflows using code and terminal tools, including analyzing data, running simulations, and fitting models. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high among the models compared at 64.6%, versus 52.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, at approximately 31% lower estimated API cost. At a lower-cost setting, Astra scores 61.1%, versus GPT-5.6 Sol’s best result of 22.4%, at approximately 27% lower estimated API cost.

tabs.label: ARC-AGI-3
captions: ARC-AGI-3 tests how well agents learn as they solve unfamiliar interactive tasks. GPT-6 Astra saturates the eval, scoring 99.9%. The average human tester scored 48%. GPT-6 Astra was measured with our responses API harness, which better reflects real-world performance than the original benchmark harness, which discards past reasoning and past messages. With this harness, we estimate Sol would score in the ballpark of ~30%.

tabs.label: FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2)
captions: FrontierMath Tier 4 tests advanced mathematical reasoning on exceptionally difficult problems.

tabs.label: Terminal-Bench 4.0
captions: Terminal-Bench 4.0 tests agents on complex terminal-based tasks, including software engineering, system configuration, and data analysis. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high at 57.9%, compared with 37.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol[[fn:2]] and 55.8% for Claude Fable 5.1, at approximately 9% and 63% lower estimated API cost per task, respectively.

tabs.label: AutomationBench
captions: AutomationBench tests whether agents can complete multistep business workflows across applications. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high among the reported results, completing 41.4% of tasks, compared with 31.4% for Claude Fable 5.1 and 26.9% for Claude Opus 5.

tabs.label: Agents’ Last Exam
captions: Agents’ Last Exam tests agents on complex professional tasks in real software, from financial modeling to engineering and media production. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high in the comparison shown, scoring 59.3%, compared with 55.5% for Claude Opus 5 and 53.6% for GPT-5.6 Sol. At these highest-scoring settings, Astra also uses approximately 65% fewer output tokens than Opus 5.

tabs.label: ScreenSpot-Pro
captions: ScreenSpot-Pro tests whether models can locate the correct interface element in high-resolution screenshots of professional software. GPT-6 Astra sets a new high with 92.7% accuracy.

tabs.label: OSWorld
captions: OSWorld 2.0 tests whether models can complete tasks by operating computer applications. Astra achieves higher task scores than any other available model with substantially fewer output tokens than GPT-5.6 Sol.

tabs.label: BenchCAD
captions: BenchCAD tests whether models can reconstruct 3D objects from multi-view renders by generating CAD code. With tools, GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high in the comparison shown, achieving a 95.9% geometric-overlap score, versus 83.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 84.3% reported for Claude Fable 5.1.[[fn:5]] Estimated API cost is approximately 43% lower than Sol and 86% lower than Fable 5.1 in the configurations shown.

tabs.label: BrowseComp
captions: BrowseComp tests deep web research through difficult questions that require finding and connecting information across websites. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high in the single-agent comparison shown, scoring 91.5%, compared with 90.8% for Claude Opus 5 and 87.4% for Claude Fable 5. At a lower-cost setting, Astra also exceeds GPT-5.6 Sol’s highest score at lower estimated API cost.

tabs.label: OpenScore String Quartets
captions: Astra can also help with specialized tasks such as digitizing sheet music. On OpenScore String Quartets (Legato camera subset), it transcribes scans of public-domain, 19th-century scores into structured digital notation that can be edited in music software. GPT-6 Astra reduces normalized transcription edit distance from 0.813 for GPT-5.6 Sol to 0.159—an 81% reduction—helping reduce manual transcription for musicians, educators, and researchers working with existing scores.[[fn:6]][[fn:7]]

tabs.label: Design Tasks (Internal)
captions: This internal evaluation tests professional brand-design work, from interpreting a brief and incorporating client feedback to creating and refining visual assets. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high of 50.0%, compared with 47.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 34.7% for Claude Fable 5.1.

tabs.label: Data Science Tasks (Internal)
captions: This evaluation tests agents’ ability to analyze incomplete, noisy business data, investigate changes in retention, usage, and revenue, and develop recommendations. GPT-6 Astra sets a new high of 40.9%.

tabs.label: FrontierCode 1.1 Extended
captions: FrontierCode 1.1 Extended evaluates whether coding agents produce changes ready to merge into real codebases. GPT-6 Astra nearly matches Claude Fable 5’s best score—64.5% versus 64.9%—at approximately 63% lower estimated API cost.[[fn:8]]

tabs.label: DeepSWE
captions: DeepSWE v1.1 tests complex software-engineering tasks in real codebases. GPT‑6 Astra scores 74.1%, compared with 72.7% for GPT‑5.6 Sol and 67.4% reported for Claude Fable 5.1. At their highest-scoring settings, Astra outperforms Sol at approximately 32% lower estimated API cost per task.

tabs.label: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent
captions: The Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index evaluates coding agents on implementing changes, fixing bugs, completing terminal-based tasks, and answering questions about existing codebases. GPT-6 Astra in Codex achieves performance comparable to the leading Claude configurations shown while using substantially fewer total tokens per task.

tabs.label: Database Migration Tasks (Internal)
captions: This internal evaluation tests database-migration work, including implementation, code review, and performance analysis. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high of 63.9%, compared with 57.8% for Claude Fable 5.1 and 42.7% for GPT-5.6 Sol. At a lower-cost setting, Astra scores 63.4%, exceeding Sol’s best result at approximately 38% lower estimated API cost.

tabs.label: GPQA Diamond
captions: GPQA Diamond tests graduate-level scientific reasoning in biology, chemistry, and physics. GPT-6 Astra reaches a new high in the comparison shown at 96.0%. At a lower-cost setting, it also exceeds GPT-5.6 Sol’s best score—94.9% versus 94.6%—at approximately 37% lower estimated API cost.

tabs.label: HealthBench Professional
captions: HealthBench Professional evaluates responses to clinicians’ requests, including care consultations, medical documentation, and research. GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest length-adjusted score among the models shown, at 63.4, compared with 60.5 for GPT-5.6 Sol. At its lowest-cost setting shown, Astra already surpasses Sol’s best score at approximately 53% lower estimated API cost.[[fn:11]]

tabs.label: LifeSciBench
captions: LifeSciBench evaluates scientific reasoning across life-sciences research tasks, including interpreting evidence, designing experiments, and troubleshooting research problems. On the Gold v1 task set, GPT-6 Astra achieves a score of 60.3, compared with 59.9 for GPT-5.6 Sol, delivering comparable performance at approximately 62% lower estimated API cost. Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 are not included in LifeSciBench Gold v1, GeneBench Pro v13, and MedChemBench because they refuse the majority of questions in these evaluations.[[fn:12]]

tabs.label: GeneBench Pro
captions: GeneBench Pro tests whether agents can analyze complex biological data, select appropriate methods and adapt their approach as findings emerge. Astra achieves higher success rates than GPT-5.6 Sol at comparable API cost. Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 are not included in LifeSciBench Gold v1, GeneBench Pro v13, and MedChemBench because they refuse the majority of questions in these evaluations.[[fn:12:2]]

tabs.label: MedChemBench
captions: MedChemBench tests medicinal-chemistry reasoning through questions involving chemical structures, quantitative predictions and scientific explanations. Astra satisfies a greater share of the evaluation’s weighted scoring criteria than previous OpenAI models at comparable API cost. Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 are not included in LifeSciBench Gold v1, GeneBench Pro v13, and MedChemBench because they refuse the majority of questions in these evaluations.[[fn:12:3]]
